project.name: Kilmany
project.boundarySource: Resolved named-place location with a conservative strict settlement study buffer
project.researchNotes: Kilmany earns a map marker from its own village identity and walkable heritage, not from Cupar or roadside businesses elsewhere. Strict-boundary score verified sequentially on 2026-09-02. The Jim Clark Motorsport Museum is in Duns, not Kilmany. Cairnie Fruit Farm and other cafés beyond the village boundary are not transferred. On-street route-start parking is not represented as a dedicated visitor car park.

touristAppeal.label: Notable Stop
touristAppeal.summary: Kilmany is a genuine notable stop: the village-centre Jim Clark statue, strong historic fabric and two documented walking routes create a coherent short visit. The absence of a café, public toilet, formal picnic site and dedicated visitor car park keeps it in the 60–69 band.
touristAppeal.dogAccessSummary: The audited outdoor routes can suit responsible dog visits, with close control around livestock, roads, wildlife and historic fabric.

features.name: Kilmany Grange
features.fullDescription: 1810, built for Dr Chalmers. 2-storey 3-window whin rubble in uneven coursed, droved dressings, margin and railed steps to door. 2-storey piended back wing, small single-storey wing on E with bipartite. Original woodwork, chimneys replaced in brick. 2 blocks of offices with quoin angles at rear, one roofless.

features.name: Keeper's Cottage, The Wynd, Kilmany
features.fullDescription: Late 18th and mid 19th century. Single-storey, 5-bay cottage (2-bays to left are 19th century). Whin rubble with sandstone dressings. Door to forth bay. Former doorway with rubble infill to second bay. Flat-roofed outshot to rear. 8-pane glazing to timber sash and case windows. Pantiles to roof. Ashlar skews. Three coped stacks with clay cans.

features.name: Kilmany House
features.fullDescription: Reginald Fairlie 1914-19 and 1927 incorporating parts of former inn for Col W. Anstruther Gray. Cape Dutch syle, harled and pantiled. 2-storey stepped L-plan with octagonal dining room at W. end, centre part has curvilinear gables and 2-arch 'stoep'. Later alteration at NW.

features.name: Kilmany Parish Church
features.fullDescription: Dated 1768, little altered. Rectangular plan, harled with margins, bird cage bellcote W gable. 3 round arched and keyblocked windows S wall, centre narrower with (blocked) minister's door below, with low square headed window on W and door on EW lean-to porch early 19th century; 2 square-headed windows N wall probably of same date original glazing throughout. Interior; lofts E and W, fine original oak pulpit with R doric entablature sounding board supported by pilasters. Reseated 1859 by Jack of Rathillet and considerably repaired with advice from David Rhind 1860-1; boarded ceiling probably dates from that time. Some fragments of 17th century oak panelling.
